feedback_history.therapist_response:
I’ve been avoiding stepping outside for days—ever since that cat touched my legs. I’d just stand there, frozen, thinking about how the fur might have carried rabies, even though it didn’t scratch me. I’ve started checking my daughter’s arms every few hours, just to see if the red dots are still there. I’ll go to the bathroom and look, or I’ll check the mirror. I don’t even know if they’re real, but I can’t stop thinking they’re from a bat bite.  

And the ER visits—last month I went because I thought I had a heart attack. I was so panicked, I thought I had a blockage. I know doctors said it was just acid reflux, but I still feel like something’s wrong. It’s like my body and my mind are telling different stories, and I don’t know which one to trust anymore.  

I don’t know if I’m just overthinking, or if something deeper is going on

feedback_history.therapist_response:
It sounds like your body and mind are carrying a lot of tension—especially with those moments when you’re afraid to go outside or check on your daughter. The way you’re holding onto those red dots, or how you freeze when the cat touches your legs, it feels like your brain is trying to protect you from something real, even if it’s not. And that ER visit—thinking you had a heart attack—must have been terrifying. It’s not just about the fear; it’s about how deeply those thoughts live in you, like they’re part of your body’s language now.  

Would it be helpful to explore what that fear feels like when it comes up—like, what happens in your body, or what kind of thoughts come first?
